subject: Follow-up: Autoscale + SLO constraints — fast-path activation and warm pool behavior
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: Autoscale + SLO constraints — fast-path activation and warm pool behavior

Thanks for your time today, Ethan — appreciate the clear rundown of Acme Cloud's production profile and the traffic burst patterns. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- SLOs you called out: p95 latency <= 180ms for streaming responses (token-by-token), p99 <= 700ms; sustained throughput target ~1,200 rps for short prompts (~150 tokens).
- Bursts: typical 20–40% of total traffic for 3–7 minute windows; rare sustained spikes up to 3x for ~10–15 minutes during product launches.
- Warm pool requirement: you prefer a warm pool that can activate instances in <45s to keep p95 under 200ms. You also expressed interest in a fast-path activation that can serve degraded streaming output while the full KV cache warms.

Questions we have for triage so we can size the pilot and put together a short validation plan: 
1) Do you have an allowed jitter on p95 for the first 60s of a burst while caches populate? (e.g., a 20–30% acceptable uplift)
2) Are there particular endpoints or routes that must not degrade (billing/checkouts) vs. ones where degraded streaming is acceptable? Please call them out by API route or product flow.
3) For warm pool sizing: confirm whether you want instance-level pre-warmed kernels (recommended) or just a lightweight slot reservation with faster boot orchestration — we can propose both.

Attached is a short template to capture the SLOs and a one-page sketch of our fast-path proposal. If that looks good I suggest a 60-minute technical dry-run with Ben and Neha next week to agree test harness and metrics. Proposed windows: Tue/Wed morning PST.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
(415) 555-0129

Attachments: acme-slo-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub) ; rdw-autoscale-proposal-v1.pdf (one-page sketch)

From: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@acmecloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Autoscale + SLO constraints — fast-path activation and warm pool behavior

Thanks Laura — useful summary. A few clarifications from our ops team: 

- Jitter tolerance: During the first 90s of a burst we can tolerate up to 35% uplift at p95 for non-critical flows. For checkout/billing flows we need to ensure p95 < 250ms at all times; p99 can be relaxed to 900ms for 2 minutes if we show graceful degradation.
- Critical endpoints: /api/v1/checkout, /api/v1/payment/authorize, /api/v1/account/lookup are high priority. All user-chat endpoints can accept partial streaming (token flush every 200ms) while the full model cache warms.
- Warm pool preference: pre-warmed kernels + lightweight KV cache snapshotting preferred if possible — we expect a mix of large (>40GB KV) and small (<8GB KV) request patterns.

I've attached our SLO worksheet filled out and a short PDF describing our launch-day traffic expectations. If you can propose a test matrix (latency ramps, warm pool kills, capacity failover), we can schedule the dry-run as early as Wed 09:00 PST.

-Ethan
Ethan Ross
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Cloud
ethan.ross@acmecloud.com

Attachments: acme-slo-requirements.xlsx (updated worksheet); streaming-requirements-notes.pdf

Forwarding Acme's completed SLO worksheet and clarifications. Key asks: 
- p95 streaming <= 180ms baseline, must keep checkout flows <250ms even during bursts.
- Warm pool: prefer pre-warmed kernels + KV snapshot approach; activation <45s target.
- Tolerance: up to 35% p95 uplift first 90s for non-critical flows.

Proposed internal next steps: 
1) Ben: can you draft a short test matrix (latency ramp, kernel warm sequencing, KV snapshot restore, and streaming degraded-mode)? Aim for a reproducible harness that runs in our staging cluster.
2) Neha: advise on warm pool sizing and whether we should propose a hybrid: small pre-warmed fleet + fast boot slots for peak. Include cost delta estimate.
3) Jordan: I'll need a short runbook snippet for canary/fallback (route to smaller/cheaper model variant vs. queueing).

Let's aim to send Acme a 1-week pilot plan and calendar invite for Wed 09:00 PST. Ben/Neha — are you available?

Thanks,
Laura

Laura / team — I can take point on the test matrix. Draft outline below: 

A) Perf matrix (staging):
  1) Baseline latency profile (no warm pool, steady 300 rps) -- measure p50/p95/p99 for small/large prompts.
  2) Warm pool activation test: kill warm pool instances and measure 0–120s activation curve; capture p95 uplift.
  3) KV snapshot restore vs incremental populate: compare full-restore time and token output quality during restore.
  4) Streaming degraded-mode: enable token-flush every 200ms, record user-perceived latency and dropped tokens.
  5) Burst replay: 1x -> 3x spike for 10/15 minutes, validate autoscale ramp and fallback routing.

B) Success criteria (pilot):
  - For non-critical routes: p95 <= 250ms after 90s; p99 <= 1.2s.
  - For critical routes: p95 <= 250ms at all times; any p95 >250ms must trigger immediate fallback to smaller variant.
  - Warm pool activation 90% of test runs <45s from decision -> first byte.

I'll assemble the harness (k6 + custom tokenized playback) and share the repo link by EOD tomorrow.

-Ben

Attachment: rdw-autoscale-proposal-v1.pdf (internal copy)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Autoscale + SLO constraints — fast-path activation and warm pool behavior

I'm good to join Wed 09:00 PST. Quick notes from a sizing/cost POV: 

- Hybrid warm pool recommendation: keep ~15% of expected steady-state capacity in pre-warmed kernels (smaller instances for cost efficiency) + an on-demand fast-boot slot group sized for 1.5x average burst capacity. The idea: keep p95 low for first 30–45s via pre-warmed, use fast-boot + KV snapshotting to raise to peak.
- Estimate: for Acme's stated steady-state (1,200 rps) that maps to ~12 mid-gpu instances pre-warmed; cost delta vs pure on-demand warm pool ~12% over baseline, likely justified for launch-day SLAs.
- Ops note: we should include a metric for first-token latency (FTL) and stream-chunk cadence (target <=200ms chunk flush) in the success criteria.

I will prepare a short slide with cost delta and a warm-pool sizing table for the pilot plan.

-Neha
